source_text: 53.1. Ergo cum haec ita sint, non absone neque inaniter credimus, mediae qualitatis esse animas hominum utpote ab rebus non principalibus editas, iuri subiectas mortis, parvarum et labilium virium: perpetuitate donari, <si> spem muneris tanti deum ad principem conferant, cui soli potestas est talia corruptione exclusa largiri. 2. ''Sed stulte istud credimus''. - Quid ad vos, <si> ineptissime, fatue? Ubi vobis nocemus vel quam vobis facimus aut inrogamus iniuriam, si omnipotentem confidimus deum habiturum esse rationem nostri, cum abire a corporibus coeperimus et ab Orci faucibus quemadmodum dicitur [Liv. IX,6] vindicari?
pass_a_gloss: Souls mediae qualitatis—not from principal things, subject to death, small/labile powers. Perpetuitas only if they set spes of so great a gift on deum principem, who alone can give such with corruptione exclusa. You call it stulte—but where is your injury if we trust omnipotens deus will reclaim us from Orci fauces?
pass_b_english: 53.1. Therefore since these things are so, we believe not discordantly nor emptily that human souls are of a middle quality, as brought forth from things not principal, subject to the law of death, of small and slipping powers: that they are gifted with perpetuity if they bring the hope of so great a gift to God the prince, to whom alone belongs the power to bestow such things with corruption shut out. 2. "But we believe that foolishly." — What is that to you, if most ineptly, stupidly? Where do we harm you, or what injury do we do or inflict on you, if we trust that almighty God will have regard for us when we begin to leave bodies and, as it is said, be claimed from the jaws of Orcus?

lemmas.sense: subject to the law of death
gift from God the prince alone

choices.choose: Hold immortality as gift from God the prince, not natural soul-rank
choices.why: mediae qualitatis ... perpetuitate donari si ... deum ad principem

choices.choose: Trust God to reclaim from death without harming pagan neighbors
choices.reject: Christian hope as injury to others
choices.why: ubi vobis nocemus ... omnipotentem ... ab Orci faucibus ... vindicari

notes: Grace-and-assistance: mid-quality mortal souls receive perpetuity only by gift from God the prince.
